recognize_zh: Perls 鐵染色（紅色對比染色）下，數顆紅血球母細胞的核周圍排列著藍黑色鐵顆粒，呈部分或完整環狀（ring sideroblasts）；背景有大量針狀結晶樣染色沉澱物，影像對焦有限。
features: Erythroblasts (red counterstained nuclei) with coarse blue-black iron granules arranged around the nuclear rim
Several cells show perinuclear granules encircling a substantial part of the nucleus (ring sideroblasts)
Occasional larger dark iron aggregates adjacent to cells
Background of needle-like crystalline precipitate, likely stain/processing artifact
Suboptimal focus limits counting of granules per cell
describe_en: Perls Prussian blue stain of a bone marrow aspirate smear, shown in a main field and two insets, highlights erythroblasts with coarse blue-black siderotic granules arranged in a perinuclear distribution, encircling a substantial portion of the nucleus in several cells, consistent with ring sideroblasts. The background contains abundant needle-like crystalline precipitate, most likely stain artifact, and the image is somewhat out of focus, which limits precise counting. Formal quantification (percentage of ring sideroblasts among erythroblasts, with at least five granules covering one third of the nuclear circumference) should be performed on a well-stained smear. Findings are consistent with sideroblastic anemia, in this case X-linked sideroblastic anemia.

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts contain only a few fine granules scattered randomly in the cytoplasm rather than coarse granules encircling the nucleus.
Ring sideroblasts look identical; separation relies on age, multilineage dysplasia, SF3B1 mutation versus ALAS2 or other germline mutations.

ddx.dx: Acquired reversible sideroblastic states (alcohol, copper deficiency, isoniazid, zinc toxicity)
ddx.vs: Ring sideroblasts are morphologically similar, so history, copper/zinc levels and drug exposure are required to distinguish them.
